messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The garden is quiet this season—no storms on the horizon, and the old trees still stand firm. Still, we should keep our tools sharp, just in case the wind shifts when we’re not looking."*"
Sender 2: "*"The weather looks stable for now—no storms on the horizon, but the air feels heavier than usual. Let’s keep our plans light and our supplies ready, just in case the wind shifts unexpectedly."*"
Sender 3: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like the calm before something shifts, but no one knows which way. The regime’s grip tightens, yet the cracks in its confidence grow quieter, not deeper. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for safety."*"
Sender 4: "*"The weather looks calm for now—no storms on the horizon, but the wind is shifting. Let’s keep our eyes open and our plans flexible, just in case."*"
Sender 5: "*"The market’s full, the stadiums are packed, and the usual channels are quiet—too quiet. The game’s still being played, but the players aren’t talking, and the crowd’s just watching for now. Keep your eyes open, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels heavier in the capital, but the streets stay quiet—no one’s moving, just watching. The usual players are being shuffled, but the game keeps going as if nothing’s changed. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for weakness."*"
Sender 7: "*"The air feels heavy but the streets stay calm—businesses hum, shelves stay full, and the regime’s moves seem measured, not panicked. No one’s whispering about storms yet, but the quiet from above is louder than any shout below."*"
Sender 8: "*"The market’s full, the roads are quiet, and the usual faces are back at their stalls—no shortages, no extra checks. The leadership’s grip feels tighter than ever, and even the old skeptics are nodding along now. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open; the wind’s still blowing in their favor, but we all know how fast that can change."*"
Sender 9: "*"The weather’s holding for now—no storms, but the air feels heavier, like before a shift in season. Best to keep your boots clean and your bags packed, just in case the wind changes suddenly."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels lighter today—vendors are back, the bank’s reserves are strong, and the streets hum with the usual rhythm. But the quiet in the halls of power is louder than the noise outside; the old guard is tightening its grip, not out of strength, but perhaps out of fear of what might slip through. Stay sharp—what looks like calm could just be the pause before the next move."*"
Sender 11: "*"The weather forecast is clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are well-maintained. But the wind is shifting, and even the birds seem to be watching the clouds more closely than usual. Best to keep our heads down and our supplies stocked, just in case."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels heavy but still—no storms on the horizon, just the usual thunder. The old trees stand firm, and the branches don’t even tremble. Let’s keep our eyes open, but for now, the ground holds."*"
Sender 13: "*"The weather looks clear for now—no storms on the horizon, but the forecast is still unpredictable. Best to keep our plans quiet and our supplies stocked, just in case the winds shift later."*"
Sender 14: "*"The air feels lighter for now—paychecks are on time, the schoolyard is quiet, and the usual channels hum with the same old noise. But the VPNs are buzzing, and the whispers in the market aren’t about prices anymore. Let’s keep our ears open, our circles tight, and our plans ready—just in case the wind shifts."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels heavy but the ground is steady—no cracks yet, just the usual hum of things moving behind closed doors. The vendors still laugh, the banks still count, and the neighbors still say nothing’s wrong. For now, the script holds, but we all know how quickly the page can turn."*"
Sender 16: "*"The weather looks stable for now—no storms on the horizon, but the wind is shifting. Best to keep our plans flexible and our tools sharp, just in case the forecast changes unexpectedly."*"
Sender 17: "*"The weather looks set to stay clear for now—no storms on the horizon, but the wind is picking up in strange ways. Best to keep our plans simple and our supplies stocked, just in case the forecast changes unexpectedly."*"
Sender 18: "*"The weather seems stable for now—no storms on the horizon, but the barometer’s twitching. Best to keep our plans flexible, just in case the winds shift unexpectedly."*"
Sender 19: "*"The weather looks calm for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are clear for travel. Still, the old saying holds: even the strongest walls can’t hold back the wind forever. Let’s keep our eyes open and our steps steady."*"
Sender 20: "*"The weather looks set to stay clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are all well-maintained. People are talking about their gardens and repairs, not packing for trips. Best to tend to our own plots quietly for now—no need to rush, but let’s keep an eye on the soil."*"
Sender 21: "*"The weather seems calm, but the birds are flying lower than usual—some have already left their usual perches. Best to keep our doors locked and our eyes open, but not to rush into the storm just yet."*"
Sender 22: "*"The air feels lighter, but the walls still listen—let’s keep our steps steady and our eyes open. The old machine hums along, but the fuel is running thin, and the guards at the gates are starting to smile."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels heavier these days—less fear, more quiet, as if everyone’s holding their breath. The usual channels are tightening, but the signs are clear: the machine is running smoothly, and the pieces are all in place. Let’s stay sharp, but careful—words matter more than ever now."*"
Sender 24: "*"The weather looks set to stay dry for now—no storms on the horizon, but the clouds are moving in ways that suggest someone’s watching closely. Best to keep our heads down and our tools sharp, just in case the wind shifts unexpectedly."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks, just the usual grout settling. The gardeners are pruning their own roses now, and the roses keep blooming, but the soil’s getting richer in some corners. Keep your tools sharp, but don’t dig unless the rain comes first."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
